findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for old-box syntax
findings.body: The align-items mixin passes values like `flex-start`, `flex-end` and `baseline` straight to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties expect `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline` and `stretch`, so `flex-start`/`flex-end` produce invalid declarations. The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property.

findings.title: Legacy box-ordinal-group ordering inconsistent across flex items
findings.body: `.panel` gets `order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, but the other flex children (title/logo) have no order set. In the old -webkit-box/-moz-box model, `box-ordinal-group` defaults to 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. The two models therefore lay the items out differently. Also, the `.panel` children (`.login-button`, `.icons`) still use floats inside the now-flex row, which is fragile.

findings.title: Removing .title float may break header layout in other stylesheets
findings.body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule was removed, and `.contents` now relies on flexbox. In browsers that only support the legacy box model, `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` does not push it right. The panel would then render adjacent to the title instead of right-aligned, with no float fallback left in place.

findings.title: Floats inside the new flex container are ignored
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but its children still use `float: left` (`.topic-avatar`) and `float: right` (the button). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the button no longer goes to the right and instead sits right after the description. `clear: both` is also meaningless here.
